title: Dedicated capacity boundary evidence orchestrator for tenant isolation proofs
creator: Aisha M. Patel
description:
Build an automated orchestration service that collects, signs, and exports verifiable boundary evidence for Dedicated capacity tenants to satisfy data-residency and tenant-isolation attestations. The orchestrator will assemble node- and network-level artifacts (instance IDs, AZ/region tags, VPC/subnet attachments, disk mount identifiers, kernel version, container image digest, attached GPU identifiers), combine them with recent audit-log slices, and produce a signed, time-windowed evidence bundle that can be delivered to customers or stored for audits. This ticket covers the orchestration, signing, retention controls, and an export pipeline; UI surface and long-term archival retention policy are separate tickets.

Scope in this ticket: implement the collector + evidence manifest format, KMS/HSM signing integration, per-tenant export endpoint (S3 pre-signed or secure SFTP), monthly and on-demand run modes, retention enforcement hooks that connect to existing retention config service, and basic Console telemetry hooks.

Out of scope: design of Console UI pages (tracked in PM-502), legal language for attestations, and enterprise SLA contract issuance flows.

Why: customers frequently request auditable proof that their Dedicated capacity is physically and logically isolated. Manual evidence assembly is error-prone and slow — automation reduces time-to-delivery and enables scheduled compliance exports.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Orchestrator can collect required node+network artifacts from any active dedicated node and assemble a single JSONL evidence manifest per tenant window.
2) Manifest is signed with customer-scoped KMS keys (supporting HSM-backed keys) and stores a signature envelope and key ID.
3) Evidence export supports: a) tenant-specific S3 upload with server-side encryption, b) on-demand pre-signed URL generation with 24h TTL, and c) drop to secure SFTP endpoint.
4) Retention settings respect tenant-configured retention policy (min/max bounds enforced) and a retention label is embedded in the manifest.
5) Audit logs linking the collector run, signature, and export are emitted to the central audit topic and are queryable by trace ID.
6) Unit and integration tests cover collector, manifest formatter, signer, and exporter.
7) Security review sign-off obtained and documented in the ticket.
8) End-to-end demo script and post-mortem checklist checked into Confluence.
comments: 2025-02-16 - Marcus: Spike completed. Collector prototype gathers instance metadata, attached volumes, and docker image digests from the dedicated-node agent. Found variability in GPU vendor reporting; need a small adapter layer.

2025-02-20 - Aisha (PM): Compliance asked for signed chain-of-custody and explicit retention TTL in the manifest. They prefer HSM-backed keys for high-risk customers. See Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COM/Boundary+Evidence+Spec

2025-02-24 - Marcus: Decided trade-off: do periodic (daily) signed bundles by default plus on-demand runs to avoid steady-state CPU/KMS usage. Real-time signing of each request was rejected due to KMS cost and latency. Added background job queue to batch signing operations in 5-minute windows.

2025-02-28 - Security review (Sanjay R.): Reviewed key usage patterns. Recommend adding key-rotation metadata to manifest and requiring encrypt-in-transit on all exporter targets. Created follow-up: ENG-22512 (key-rotation enforcement).

2025-03-05 - Marcus: Integration PR opened for the collector and manifest writer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1456. Initial CI failing on HSM emulator integration (test certificate path mismatch).
2025-03-09 - QA (Lena): Integration smoke tests green on staging. Verified signed manifest verifies against KMS public key. Minor schema change: add 'sequence_id' to support incremental proof chains.
2025-03-10 - Marcus: Paired with Console team to add a telemetry hook (tenant.attestation_run) — Console ticket PM-510 will read these traces for the Compliance tab.
implementation_notes: Manifest format chosen is JSONL with one canonicalized JSON per line and a separate envelope file with signature metadata (key_id, algorithm, timestamp, sequence_id). We will include Merkle-root of included artifacts for compact verification. Collector runs will be idempotent; artifacts have stable identifiers (instance-id, disk-uuid). Exports use tenant-specific buckets with enforced bucket policies and SSE-KMS. For HSM-backed signing, the signer will use a short lived CSR/session and never persist private key material on disk.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KMS/HSM throughput limits could delay on-demand attestations. Mitigation: batch-signing windows and async pre-warm for customers with SLA needs. Risk: incomplete metadata on older dedicated nodes. Mitigation: agent update rollout (ENG-22605) and fallback to network-level evidence. Risk: retention misconfiguration could violate contracts — enforce min retention guardrails and require PM/legal approval for deviations.
next_steps: 1) Merge PR for collector & manifest writer. 2) Add HSM emulator fix and re-run CI (ENG-22590). 3) Implement exporter adapters and add E2E tests. 4) Schedule security review on 2025-03-12. 5) Demo to Compliance on 2025-03-18.
notes: Goal is to produce artifacts that customers can independently verify without requiring Redwood to run ad-hoc queries. Use canonicalized manifest + public key publication in a customer-specific metadata endpoint. Ensure all artifacts are covered by existing audit retention policies.
